![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/501a3512fb4b8a1898c6dfb8816d587de4a0cd585991d9c92d2bb35d83a2853d.png)

Consider the vector field $F(x,y)$ shown above. Let $C$ be the path where the semicircle is traversed from $A$ to $B.$ Which of the following statements are true?

I. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$

II. ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0$

III. ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0$
question.worked_solution:
Remember that ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r$ gives the total work done by a force $F$ in moving a particle along $C:$

- If the force works *with* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force helps to push the particle along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

- If the force works *against* the motion of the particle (i.e., the force impedes the motion of the particle as it moves along the path), then ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

With that in mind, let's check each statement.

- Statement I is false while statement II is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ works against the motion of the particle as it moves from $A$ to $B.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/4c11b38f9e598e0cd8fc50715d2091e5bea48d188440ae8a99c84d66a6acb6b9.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r<0.$

- Statement III is true. It's clear from the picture below that $F$ assists the motion of the particle as it moves from $B$ to $A.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14228741/assets/346007ae582fccdf4519a3d1cd50a467e19d5345238343a1311fd3348bbeb138.png)

 
So, ${\int }_{-C}F\cdot \text{d}r>0.$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."
